subject: Remove repeated index reads, planner initialization, and irrelevant filesystem probes from verification guards
claim: The complete routing guard passed in 38607 ms compared with the prior 47216 ms observation. It reads the Git index once for 126 owners, reuses immutable planner initialization within eleven dependency closures, and probes only relevant retirement-inventory files. General/native routing coverage remains 31/280 cases. A quoted managed command that the old retirement scanner missed is now rejected and protected by six focused classification cases in the existing verifier.

limitations: These are single Windows observations using the existing worktree and retained tools, not controlled cold-host benchmarks or enforceable thresholds. Component timings were measured inside a PowerShell process and exclude its startup; complete verifier timing includes its own work in a fresh PowerShell process.
Linux PowerShell validation was not run: the available Debian distribution has Git but no pwsh. No cross-host performance claim is made.

The scanner comparison initially exposed a pre-existing false negative for a quoted package command. The revised scanner intentionally rejects that case; all other fixture outcomes agree. Six permanent classification cases remain in Verify-Verification-Plan.ps1; the temporary Git/index diagnostic harnesses are not new verifier entry points.

The full implementation/qualification suites were not run because changed-file planning selected only plan verification, with no native owners or coverage gaps. Compiler/runtime behavior is outside the causal scope of these setup changes.

Planner initialization is shared only within one verifier invocation. There is no persistent passing-result cache, no reuse across edits, and no omission of selected owner checks. Overall repository qualification remains incomplete and does not meet its performance target.
Peak working-set measurements cover the main PowerShell process, not aggregate child-process memory.
